body.p: Claims 1, 2, 6, 8, 9, 13, 15, 16, and 20 have been amended and new Claim 22 has been added herein. Upon the entry of the amendments, Claims 1-22 will be pending in this application. The amendments to Claims 1, 8, and 15 are supported, for example, by [0003], [0025], [0043], [0044], [0050], and [0051] of the originally filed specification, hereinafter "Specification." Applicant respectfully traverses the rejections, the characterizations of the pending claims, and any implicit and/or explicit reliance on Official Notice. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application in view of the above amendment and remarks set forth below.

Claims 1-3, 7-10, 14-17, 20, and 21 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Takeuchi et al. (U.S. Patent Pub. No. 2017/0259433, hereinafter "Takeuchi") in view of Diolaiti et al. (U.S. Patent Pub. No. 2011/0202068, hereinafter "Diolaiti").

Claims 4-6, 11-13, 18, and 19 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Takeuchi in view of Diolaiti and further in view of Nakasu et al. (U.S. Patent Pub. No. 2020/0306965, hereinafter "Nakasu").
Standard for 35 U.S.C. Q 103

The Patent and Trademark Office has the burden under 35 U.S.C. § 103 to establish aprima facie case of obviousness. The rationale to support a conclusion that the claim would have been obvious is that all the claimed elements were known in the prior art and one skilled in the art could have combined the elements as claimed by known methods with no change in their respective functions, and the combination yielded nothing more than predictable results to one of ordinary skill in the art. It can be important to identify a reason that would have prompted a person of ordinary skill in the relevant field to combine the elements in the way the claimed new invention does. If any of these findings cannot be made, then this rationale cannot be used to support a
conclusion that the claim would have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art. M.P.E.P. § 2143.

Applicant respectfully submits that the cited references do not teach the combination of elements recited in each of independent Claims 1, 8, and 15, as amended. For example, with respect to Claim 1, the cited references do not teach or suggest at least the claimed method "executed by data processing hardware of a robot including an articulated arm having an end effector engaged with a constrained object having at least one constrained axis and at least one axis of freedom" comprising "identifying, using the measured task parameter set, the at least one axis of freedom and the at least one constrained axis for the constrained object." Amended independent Claims 8 and 15 include similar features.

In rejecting previously pending Claim 1, the Examiner relies on Diolaiti as allegedly teaching "determining, using the measured task parameter set, at least one axis of freedom and at least one constrained axis for the end effector within a workspace." Office Action, page 5 (citing Diolaiti, [0039]).

Diolaiti states that "the instrument may have internal mechanical constraints (e.g., cables, gearing, cams and belts, etc.) that force multiple joints to move together in a pre-determined fashion. Each set of mechanically constrained joints implements a specific axis of motion, and constraints may be devised to pair rotational joints (e.g., joggle joints)." Diolaiti, [0039].

Based on the above, Applicant respectfully submits that Diolaiti at best relates to mechanical constraints that are internal to the instrument. Thus, Diolaiti does not teach or suggest identifying an axis of freedom nor a constrained axis of a constrained object engaged by an end effector of an articulated arm.

Thus, Diolaiti fails to teach or suggest at least the feature "identifying, using the measured task parameter set, the at least one axis of freedom and the at least one constrained axis for the constrained object" of amended independent Claim 1.

The other references were cited merely to supposedly show certain features which are unrelated to the above-indicated feature and these references do not remedy the deficiencies of Diolaiti. Therefore, the combination of the cited references does not teach or suggest all of the features of each of independent Claims 1, 8, and 15. Thus, not all claim elements were known in

the cited references. Furthermore, the Examiner did not identify a reason, at least with respect to the above-identified feature, that would have prompted a person of ordinary skill in the relevant field to combine the elements in the way the claimed invention does. In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that no prima facie case of obviousness has been established with respect to Claims 1, 8, and 15 and thus, these claims are patentable over the cited references.

Claims 2-7, 9-14, and 16-21 depend from one of base Claims 1, 8, and 15, and further define additional technical features. In view of the patentability of their base claim, and in further view of the additional technical features, Applicant respectfully submits that the dependent claims are patentable over the cited references. Furthermore, Applicant does not necessarily agree with the characterization of the cited references made by the Examiner in rejecting the dependent claims.

p.u: Discussion of Patentability of New Claim

body.p: New Claim 22 includes all of the features of base Claim 1 and further recites additional technical features. Because Claim 1 is allowable, new Claim 22 is patentable over the cited references for at least the same reasons and for the additional features.

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application.
